newsitem.title: USA: Orono, Minn., GO improvement bonds Aa1 - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Orono, Minn., GO improvement bonds Aa1 - Moody's.

text.p: Orono (City of) MN
Municipality
Minnesota
Moody's Rating
Issue
General Obligation Improvement Bonds, Series 1997 RATING
Aa1
Sale Amount $1,760,000.00
Expected Sale Date 06/23/97
Rating Description General Obligation Bonds

NEW YORK, June 19, 1997 -- Moody's has assigned a rating of Aa1 to the Orono, MN general obligation debt in conjunction with the upcoming sale of $1,760,000 General Obligation Improvement Bonds, Series 1997.
The Aa1 rating is based on the affluence of this slowly developing Minneapolis suburb, well-managed financial operations that rely principally on residential property taxes, and low debt levels.
Orono is one of the wealthiest residential suburbs in the state.

Resident median family income is nearly twice that of the state; per capita income is nearly three times that of the state; full value per capita continues to exceed $100,000, despite the lack of a significant commercial or industrial base.
Six of the top ten taxpayers are individual residences. Moody's expects the city to continue slow development of primarily wealthy single family residences.
Conservative budgeting practices have contributed to a strong financial position with General Fund reserves maintained at more than 40% of revenues.
Significant reserve levels provide for contingencies and eliminate the need for cash flow borrowing.
A 1996 operating deficit was due to unanticipated purchase of a land parcel located next to city hall which will allow the city to influence commercial development along the Highway 12 corridor.
Balanced operations are expected for fiscal year-end 1997 with year to date revenues exceeding conservative projections and expenditures.

Debt burden is low at 2.2%. Forty percent of overall debt is attributed to the issuance of four school districts. Future borrowing is limited and primarily associated with ongoing efforts to convert existing residential septic systems to the city sewer system.
A majority of outstanding debt is supported by special assessments and revenues.
We have also reviewed and assigned a Aa2 rating to the Orono Housing and Redevelopment Authority's Public Facility Revenue Bonds, Series 1991.

Bondholder security is provided by the absolute and unconditional obligation of the City of Orono to make lease payments to the authority in amounts sufficient to retire the bonds, subject to annual appropriations.

The city is able to levy an unlimited property tax to fund rental payments. The rating reflects the risk of nonappropriation and is accordingly lower than the Aa1 rating assigned to the city's general obligation bonds. ANALYSTS:
Patricia South, Analyst, Public Finance Group, Moody's Investors Service
